title: Seller's Property Condition Disclosure
description: West Virginia does not have a comprehensive statutory seller disclosure requirement like most states. However, common law requires sellers to disclose known material defects that would not be discoverable through reasonable inspection. The West Virginia Association of Realtors provides a voluntary property disclosure form that has become standard practice. Case law (Roberts v. Stevens Clinic Hospital) reinforces the duty to disclose known latent defects.

required_actions.note: While not statutorily mandated, standard practice strongly favors completing a property disclosure form. Common law duty to disclose known latent defects applies.

citations: Roberts v. Stevens Clinic Hospital, 176 W.Va. 492 (1986)
W.Va. Code §30-40-1 et seq. (Real Estate License Act)

metadata.note: West Virginia lacks a comprehensive statutory disclosure requirement; common law duty applies.

title: Attorney-Close State Requirement
description: West Virginia is an attorney-close state. The West Virginia State Bar has opined that the preparation of real estate documents, title examination, and closing supervision constitutes the practice of law. A licensed West Virginia attorney must examine title, prepare the deed, and supervise the closing. West Virginia State Bar Unauthorized Practice of Law opinions reinforce this requirement.

required_actions.note: A West Virginia licensed attorney must examine title, prepare the deed, and supervise the closing.

citations: WV State Bar UPL Advisory Op. 2003-01
Lawyer Disciplinary Bd. v. Allen, 228 W.Va. 258 (2011)

title: Agency Disclosure and Brokerage Relationships
description: West Virginia requires written disclosure of brokerage relationships at the initial contact with a prospective buyer or seller. Dual agency is permitted with written informed consent from both parties. The West Virginia Real Estate Commission requires use of the approved Disclosure of Brokerage Relationships form.

required_actions.note: Must be provided at initial contact. Dual agency consent must be documented in writing.

title: Lead-Based Paint Disclosure (Pre-1978)
description: Federal law requires disclosure of known lead-based paint hazards for residential properties built before 1978. West Virginia follows federal requirements. Sellers must provide the EPA pamphlet and allow a 10-day inspection contingency.

title: Real Estate Advertising Compliance
description: West Virginia Real Estate Commission rules require that all real estate advertising include the licensed name of the brokerage firm. Blind ads (advertising without firm identification) are prohibited. All advertising must be truthful and not misleading.

required_actions.note: All ads must include brokerage firm name as licensed. Blind ads prohibited.
